beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. A Skill is a pre-made instruction file that teaches Claude to behave for a specific task, called by slash command. The /how-to skill guides any user from zero to done on any Claude task, asking the right questions first. Install in four steps: download the file, then Customize, Skills, plus, Create skill, Upload a skill. Its core move is AskUserQuestion: Claude interviews you with three to five questions, then plans better.

beats.narration_text: Here is the artifact: a Claude Skill called /how-to. You install it from a shared skill file, upload it into Claude, and from then on you just type /how-to plus whatever you want to do with AI — and Claude walks you through it, step by step, asking you the right questions before giving you a plan. The claim is that procedural guidance can live inside the Skill instead of being rediscovered across dozens of articles.

Step back for a second: what is a Claude skill, technically? It's a pre-made prompt — a file of instructions — that teaches Claude how to behave for a specific task. You install it once, then call it by name with a slash command. No more repeating your context. No more pasting the same prompt. the /how-to skill is just that: a file that tells Claude to guide a user from zero to done on any Claude task.

The install takes four steps. Download the shared Skill file. Then inside Claude: Customize → Skills → plus sign → Create skill → Upload a skill. Select the file. Done. Open a new chat, type /how-to, add what you want to accomplish, and Claude starts asking you questions instead of waiting for a perfect prompt from you.

beats.narration_text: There's a technique inside the skill that This can be understood as out by name: AskUserQuestion. Instead of you trying to write the perfect prompt, Claude becomes the interviewer. It asks three to five targeted questions. The more you answer, the better the plan it gives back. In practice, this one move — making Claude ask YOU the questions first — puts you ahead of ninety-nine-point-nine percent of AI users. And he's not wrong.

Power users can add a stronger reasoning layer. Don't use the regular chat view. Open Claude Cowork instead. Select Opus model at High effort. Then invoke /how-to. The reasoning engine runs longer, the questions go deeper, and the plan that comes back is more thorough. Solo users get a fine result in Chat mode — but Cowork plus Opus is the ceiling. That's the strongest stack for running the skill.
